function: Excluded (system): Byzantine-robust over-the-air FL aggregation (device clustering and weighting) over a scalar single-antenna channel without RIS (p. 3, eq. 4).
notes: PDF is the arXiv v1 preprint (2503.18284v1) titled 'Byzantine-Resilient Over-the-Air Federated Learning under Zero-Trust Architecture'; the DOI is not printed in it, matched by topic and venue. Excluded with code system. Checks 1-5 pass: it is a research article proposing FedSAC; in federated learning over the air the learned element is the MLP/CNN trained across the devices (p. 10); the problem is the over-the-air aggregation itself (hierarchical AirComp with device clustering and weighting factors, pp. 2-3), which the paper calls confined to the physical layer (p. 10). The link is single-antenna: eq. (4) on p. 3 uses a scalar fading h_{m,k} ~ CN(0,1) between the PS and each device plus large-scale fading beta_k; the text never mentions antenna arrays, MIMO, or a RIS (beamforming and RIS appear only in related-work citations, p. 1 and refs. [17], [22], [23], [51]). So an area 7 work with a single-antenna link and no RIS meets rule 6. Alternative for the reviewer: the clustering, weighting, and reputation-based Byzantine identification are not learned and could be read as security outside the seven areas (function). The code is on GitHub (p. 10, ref. [53] on p. 15); baselines are random clustering and non-robust AirFL; no criteria were charted because the work is excluded.
